transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Raj Patel (Redwood) — Dana Morales, Ethan Brooks, Priya Singh, Tom Watkins, Lena Ortiz (Silvercrest)
Links shared: onboarding playbook (link), security pack (link to SOC2 + ISO summary), sample benchmark spreadsheet (link)

Summary: quick intro, scope pilot (3-4 services), network/security constraints, decision between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private later; agree next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thank you for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE working with Silvercrest on onboarding. Quick round robin, who do we have?
[00:08] Dana Morales: Dana here, head of platform at Silvercrest, i'll be the main technical sponsor.
[00:12] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, eng mgr, i'll be helping on integration and infra.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Priya, security lead. we'll have questions on encryption and audit logs.
[00:20] Tom Watkins: Tom, DevOps, i'll share network details.
[00:25] Lena Ortiz: Lena, product, will own pilot success criteria.
[00:30] Liam O'Neill: Liam, I'm the CSM at Redwood, i'll drive the onboarding timeline and coord.
[00:35] Raj Patel: Raj, solutions engineer, i'll run the tech deep dives and benchmarks.

[02:05] Maya Chen: Great, agenda — quick intros, high level of how Redwood fits in (hosted api, dedicated, private), review security/compliance, pilot scoping, next steps. Any additions?
[02:15] Dana Morales: Nope sounds good. Our main things are latency under 350ms for chat endpoints, data residency in us-east, and SOC2 evidence. Also cost is a factor but initially reliability is more important.
[02:28] Maya Chen: makes sense. On latency — for hosted we usually see p95 around 200-400 depending on model and prompt length, if you want predictable throughput we can discuss Dedicated pools.
[02:38] Raj Patel: yeah just to add, we do autoscaling on Dedicated and you can set burst capacity. for the pilot we recommend starting on Hosted with a small reserved pool for baseline.

[05:10] Priya Singh: on security, we need KMS integration and audit logs; does Redwood provide customer-managed keys and full audit trails? also SSO, SAML, RBAC for users.
[05:20] Liam O'Neill: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and we produce audit logs and token-level cost traces. For SSO we have SAML/SCIM and RBAC roles. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[05:42] Priya Singh: ok, also data residency — we need data to remain in us-east region and retention controls. Is Private deployment required or can Hosted meet that?
[05:55] Raj Patel: Hosted can pin region-specific infra and retention configs, but for strict regulatory control you'll want Private (VPC/on-prem). For the pilot Hosted with region pinning usually suffices, and we can revisit Private if you need air-gap.

[09:00] Ethan Brooks: network question — we operate in a locked-down VPC with strict egress rules. does Redwood need peering or can we do egress to Redwood endpoints?
[09:12] Tom Watkins: we also use NAT gateways and have a proxy layer.
[09:18] Raj Patel: for Hosted, typically customers allow outbound to Redwood endpoints over TLS; for Private/Dedicated we can do VPC peering or private link. we'll need your network diagram to advise precise setup.

[12:30] Maya Chen: Pilot scope proposal — suggested: 3 services (chat for support triage, embeddings for search, and a summarization job). Run for 4 weeks, gather latency/cost/quality metrics, then decide on Dedicated or Private.
[12:45] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. KPIs we'd like: p95 latency <350ms on chat, embedding 99th percentile within 200ms for batch sizes, and cost per 1k tokens below $X — we'll refine.

[15:05] Ethan Brooks: on integration — do we use Redwood SDKs or direct REST calls? we prefer SDKs for retry/streaming support.
[15:12] Raj Patel: SDKs are recommended, we have Node/Python SDKs with streaming and function-calling support. if you need, we'll provide sample code and a starter repo.

[18:50] Priya Singh: encryption at rest, how is model data handled — are prompts logged or retained? what's retention policy?
[18:58] Liam O'Neill: by default we store logs for 30 days for debugging but you can configure retention or opt out for sensitive routes. for enterprise customers we offer configurable retention and purge controls. we'll send the retention options in the security doc.

[22:10] Dana Morales: billing — is pricing usage-based during pilot? we want to forecast cost.
[22:18] Maya Chen: Pilot typically uses hosted usage pricing; we can provide estimates from sample traffic. if you commit to Dedicated we'll discuss reserved capacity pricing. we'll send a sample cost workbook.

[26:40] Tom Watkins: curious about model variants and quantization — if we choose a smaller quantized model to save cost, does Redwood manage quality regressions?
[26:50] Raj Patel: we have Redwood Optimize recommendations and quality monitoring. you can A/B between model variants and set regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. the runtime manages KV cache and continuous batching to preserve latency.

[31:00] Lena Ortiz: success criteria — what do you recommend we lock before pilot?
[31:08] Maya Chen: agree on pilot endpoints, traffic patterns (qps), KPIs (latency, error rate, cost), security signoff and network config. if those are green after 4 weeks we move to reserved Dedicated or Private planning.

[34:30] Ethan Brooks: technical deep dive — we'd like Raj to run a perf test against a representative prompt set; can we get a script?
[34:38] Raj Patel: yep i'll share a script and a small harness, we'll run on a staging dataset and collect p50/p95/p99 and token costs. expect to coordinate on firewall access for the test.

[38:20] Priya Singh: on compliance docs — please send SOC2 and ISO summary, plus the encryption attestation.
[38:28] Liam O'Neill: will do, sending the security pack and SOC2 link after call.

[41:00] Dana Morales: timeline — we aim to start pilot by 2027-01-18 and run 4 weeks. is that feasible?
[41:08] Maya Chen: yes that's reasonable; we need your network diagram this week and the pilot endpoints list. 

[44:10] Tom Watkins: we have a question on data residency for logs — where are logs physically stored?
[44:18] Raj Patel: logs are stored in region-aligned buckets controlled by the customer's tenancy; for Hosted we pin to the region requested, for Private it's inside your VPC. we'll detail this in the security doc.

[47:30] Lena Ortiz: ok to recap next steps?
[47:35] Maya Chen: recap — Maya to send onboarding playbook, security pack, and cost workbook by 2027-01-10; Raj to share perf script by 2027-01-11; Tom to share network diagram by 2027-01-12; Priya will return security questionnaire by 2027-01-13; Lena to confirm pilot KPIs by 2027-01-14. Schedule tech deep dive week of 2027-01-18. Pilot target start 2027-01-18.
[47:55] Dana Morales: thanks all.
[48:05] Ethan Brooks: thanks, talk soon.
[48:10] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[52:00] (call ended)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear — names sometimes collapsed, product names (Redwood Dedicated) transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" in a few places.

Attachments referenced: onboarding_playbook.pdf (link), redwood_security_pack.zip (link), sample_benchmark.xlsx (link)
notes: Pilot scoped to 3 endpoints (chat, embeddings, summarization). Decision to start on Hosted with region pinning, move to Dedicated/Private if needed. Security/SSO/KMS items flagged and scheduled. Next call: technical deep dive week of 2027-01-18.
